title: Forecasting Under Uncertainty at Scale
description: Practice estimating growth trajectories, decomposing forecasts, and reasoning through compounding and cohort dynamics.

interactions.prompt: A DTC brand's monthly revenue grew from $200K to $800K over 24 months. Customer acquisition cost rose from $30 to $55 in the same period. What's the key signal?

options.text: Revenue quadrupled so the business is healthy
CAC nearly doubled, suggesting growth efficiency is deteriorating fast
They should cut marketing spend immediately
The 6% monthly revenue CAGR is below average for DTC

chartData.title: Revenue vs CAC Growth Over 24 Months

interactions.prompt: A SaaS company grows ARR at 8% monthly. Using the Rule of 72, it will roughly double its ARR every ____ months.

options.text: 7 months
9 months
12 months
15 months

interactions.prompt: You're forecasting 2025 revenue for a fintech with 40% YoY growth but entering a saturating market. Do you extrapolate the trend or model a deceleration curve?

options.text: Extrapolate 40% — momentum and team execution justify it
Model deceleration — penetration rates compress growth as TAM fills
Split the difference and forecast 20% growth
Use competitor benchmarks only, ignore historical trend

interactions.prompt: A meal-kit company reports: Month-1 retention 60%, Month-3 retention 30%, Month-6 retention 25%, Month-12 retention 23%. What does this cohort curve tell you about forecasting LTV?

options.text: LTV is unpredictable because early churn is too high
The curve flattens after month 3, so residual cohort LTV is estimable
23% annual retention means the business will fail
You need 24 months of data before any LTV estimate

interactions.prompt: Rank these factors by their impact on a 5-year revenue forecast for an enterprise SaaS company, from most to least impactful.

options.text: Net revenue retention rate (expansion vs. churn)
New logo acquisition growth rate
Average contract value trend
Sales cycle length changes

interactions.prompt: You're sizing the US electric scooter market in 2028. Your bottom-up model gives $4B but a top-down TAM approach gives $9B. How do you reconcile?

options.text: Use $9B — top-down captures adjacent demand bottom-up misses
Average them at $6.5B for a balanced view
Trust bottom-up but stress-test assumptions driving the gap
Discard both and use analyst consensus estimates instead

interactions.prompt: A ride-hailing startup asks you to forecast 3-year growth. Rank these estimation steps from first to last in a rigorous approach.

options.text: Project market share capture rate by city tier
Estimate addressable rides per day in target cities
Model cohort frequency and retention curves
Apply revenue per ride and compute annual revenue

interactions.prompt: A new competitor just raised $500M and is offering 50% subsidies in your top 3 cities, which represent 70% of revenue. How does this change your 2026 forecast?

options.text: Cut forecast 30-40% — subsidized competition compresses share and pricing
Increase forecast — competitor spending grows overall market awareness
No change — strong retention cohorts will hold steady
Pause forecasting entirely until competitive dynamics stabilize

interactions.priorContext: You previously built a 3-year ride-hailing growth forecast assuming stable competitive dynamics and steady market share gains. Now a well-funded competitor is aggressively subsidizing rides in your core markets.
